Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, one next performs repentance. Thus far, the repentance for the obstacle of afflictions has been completed; next, one repents for the obstacle of karma.
Now we shall perform repentance for the obstruction of retribution. As the Sūtra says: "Even if a hundred thousand kalpas pass, the karma of good and evil does not perish;
when the conditions and causes meet, one must receive the fruit of retribution oneself. Thus we know that the causal karma one cultivates and its resulting fruit are summoned with unerring precision.

This is why the World-Honored One manifested the ordeal of the golden spear and the horse-barley, as well as the headache from the wooden spear, so that people might have a clear and manifest model to follow.
How is this known to be so? When the five signs of impending death appear in the heavens, one is liberated from the body of a pig through repentance;

when the retribution for the five heinous crimes ripens in the human realm, the karmic penalty of hell is suddenly eliminated through remorse. Instances such as these are found throughout the scriptures; thus, we know that repentance is effective.
Truly, this can extinguish calamity. Yet I, an ordinary person, lacking the eye of the Way, how could I discern cause and effect?

I merely pursue the six sense-objects, inciting the six consciousnesses, chasing after the six external realms, and giving rise to the six internal delusions. Thus I universally commit the ten evil deeds and lose my way from the one true reality.
Since sin is created through the mutual interaction of the six sense organs, suffering in turn afflicts them through the intermingling of the six consciousnesses. What are these six?
First, the eye-organ: when the karma of seeing invites an evil retribution, this is the reciprocal retribution for seeing.

When such a person is about to die, they first see fierce fires whose blazing flames consume the void. The deceased’s spirit-consciousness rides upon the smoke, flying downward to enter the Avīci Hell, where it manifests its karmic illumination.
There are two kinds of visions. The first is clear vision: one sees everywhere evil objects—mountains of knives towering high and forests of swords reaching skyward.
The deceased’s consciousness gives rise to immeasurable fear. The second is dark vision: it is silent and nothing is seen, yet the deceased’s consciousness feels terror in its heart.
Such are the visions of fire and burning; these constitute the colors of light and darkness and the terrors of sight. As for the burning of hearing, it is as follows:
In the boiling cauldrons of molten copper, there is the sound of seething; when it burns the nose, it becomes the scent of black smoke and purple mist;
when it burns the tongue, it becomes the taste of scorched iron balls and dregs; when it burns the body, it becomes the touch of lime kilns and burning coals; and when it burns the heart...
This results in sparks scattering like fireflies and thoughts that fan the flames without ceasing. These six types [of sensations] are simultaneously experienced;
all are caused by the eye’s craving for illusory forms in the past, and such is the retribution now. If one does not repent and reform, how can there be liberation?

As for us and our assembly, from beginningless time until now, we have either craved illusory forms or become mentally attached to false sensory objects—be they the colors black, yellow, red, or purple;

crimson silk or fine gauze; rare and precious playthings; or the countenances of men and women. Chasing after such objects and seeking desirable mates, we give rise to thoughts that are contrary to the Dharma.

The commissioning of evil is inexhaustible, and the retribution it invites is as described above. Therefore, on this day, we reverently face the Triple Gem and the Compassionate Honored One, Kṣitigarbha, to repent for our past karma.
From this day forward, we shall restrain the mind to illuminate within, not pursuing external defilements, so that the true realm may manifest before us.

Seeing pure and wondrous forms, one gives rise to the wisdom of true contemplation; being unstained by the causes of habitual tendencies, one attains what was wished for and fulfills the fruit of Bodhi.
Second, regarding the retribution of hearing through repentance: due to the habituation of false hearing, one incurs evil transgressions.

When these auditory karmas intersect, at the moment of death, one first sees surging waves that submerge heaven and earth. The deceased’s consciousness descends and flows along with the current, entering into non-existence.
In the interim, two aspects are revealed: first is hearing, wherein one hears various clamors and the spirit becomes confused and disordered;

second is closed hearing, wherein all is silent and nothing is heard, and the dark soul sinks into oblivion. Such waves of hearing—when directed toward hearing, they can become reproof and interrogation;
when directed toward seeing, they can become thunder and roars; when directed toward breathing, they can become rain and mist, sprinkling all things.
Poisonous insects cover his entire body. If [the demon] pours in flavor, they turn into pus and blood, various kinds of filth;
if he pours in touch, they turn into animals and ghosts, excrement and urine; if he pours in thought, they turn into hail and sleet, crushing the heart and soul.
All such things arise from karma created through the faculty of the ear, resulting in retribution. Thus it is for myself and the assembly, since beginningless time.
In the present day, some are deluded by sounds: the notes of *gong* and *shang*, stringed instruments and pipes; the songs of Wu and the music of Zheng; theatrical performances on wooden clappers;

and male and female performers with seductive melodies and all manner of lewd lyrics. Becoming attached to these objects, their minds become bewildered, giving rise to unlawful thoughts and creating boundless transgressions.
They shall receive retribution as described above; therefore, today we openly confess and lay bare our faults, seeking compassion through repentance, and relying upon this—

Through the permeation of hearing, may my ears hear the wondrous principle of the Dharmakāya; by relying on this present method of repentance, may it immediately become the perfect sound of Prajñā’s exposition, universally transforming sentient beings so that they all return together to tranquil patience.
Third, when the retribution of smelling coincides with the ripening of habitual karma, at the moment that person’s life ends, they first see poisonous vapors filling the near and far surroundings.
The deceased’s consciousness surges up from the earth and enters the Avīci Hell, where two manifestations appear:

first, "unobstructed smelling," wherein one is permeated by various foul vapors, causing extreme mental agitation; second, "obstructed smelling," wherein the vapors suffocate and block the senses, leading to a state of fainting and collapse.
Upon the ground, smelling such odors, when the breath is struck, it can become a solid substance or a path; when sight is struck, it can become fire or a torch;
when hearing is struck, it can become sinking, drowning, melting, or boiling; when taste is struck, it can become hunger or refreshment;
when touch is struck, it can become tearing, rotting, or a great mountain of flesh with hundreds of thousands of insects all coming forth.
If one tastes food while distracted by thoughts, it can turn into ash or miasma, or into flying sand and gravel that strikes and shatters the body.

Thus, the retribution for the karma of smelling is as previously described. From beginningless time until today, I and the assembly have been deluded by the nose and committed numerous transgressions;
or, out of greed for various fragrances—sandalwood, aloeswood, *jangsu*, ox-head incense, and musk—we have fallen into error.
Camphor, clove, and horse-shoe-shaped incense; the physical forms of men and women; their tender and graceful postures—they all pursue illusory dust and create various karmas of touch.
When the retribution ripens, how can it be avoided? Therefore, today we reverently face the Triple Gem and seek compassionate repentance.
From this day forth until the end of the future, through *ānāpāna* (mindfulness of breathing), may we constantly hear of the fivefold Dharma-body.

This fragrance causes one to relinquish birth and receive birth, forever departing from the foul and impure vapors of saṃsāra. It suddenly severs the turbidity of the mundane world and perpetually increases the flavor of the Dharma.
Through śamatha and vipaśyanā, samādhi and prajñā, the ten spheres become perfectly luminous; with not a single breath of delusion, one secretly penetrates the ten stages (bhūmis).
Fourth, indulgence in flavors invites and draws forth evil retributions.

When the karmic reward for these flavors is exhausted and that person’s life comes to an end, they first see an iron net with blazing fires seething within it, enveloping the entire world. The consciousness of the deceased passes down through the iron net, which strikes its head downward and crushes it.
Entering into the Avīci Hell, two manifestations arise: first, the inhaled breath solidifies into freezing ice that freezes the flesh of the body;
second, the exhaled breath flies forth as fierce fire that burns the marrow to a pulp. Thus, regarding the retribution of taste: having experienced it, one is able to endure and bear it;
having experienced it through sight, one is able to burn metal and stone; having experienced it through hearing, it becomes like the blades of weapons.
When they pass through the breath, they can become great iron cages that completely cover the land. When they pass through contact, they can become bows and arrows, crossbows and spears.
When they pass through thought, they can become flying glowing iron that rains down from the sky, entering through the head and exiting through the feet.
Such retributions for sensory tastes are all due to the past. Having lacked faith in the Buddha-dharma, they falsely uttered words of the sages and greedily consumed wine and meat;

it is because of these actions that such retributions have been incurred. From beginningless time until now, I and the assembly have perhaps craved the blood and flesh of sentient beings—fresh, delicious, sweet, and fatty—falsely using them to sustain the four great elements, thereby further increasing the root of suffering. Like the man who boiled the tortoise and stained his fingers, we have thus given rise to enmity even between father and son.
The taste of wine startles the mind, suddenly severing the bond between sovereign and subject; because of its flavor, one creates karma—such are the transgressions involved.
How could we, the śramaṇas of the Śākya clan, ever greedily crave flavors like this? Therefore, today, standing reverently before the sages and worthies, I repent with all my heart.

From this day forth, I vow to moderate myself by eating only vegetarian food, to distance myself from all that is tainted and foul, and to constantly partake of the joy of dhyāna and the delight of the Dharma.

Fully satiated, they proclaim the Dharma through the four analytical knowledges and perform their musical offerings with the eightfold tones. Teaching the Dharma in accordance with the capacities of beings, they extend and propagate the life-force of wisdom.
Together with all sentient beings, they equally transcend attachment to the flavors of existence.

Fifth, the retribution of contact draws forth evil fruits. When the karma of contact ripens and this person is about to die, they first see great mountains closing in from all four sides, with no way out.
The deceased’s consciousness sees a great iron city, with fire-snakes and fire-dogs.
Lions, elephants, tigers, and wolves, along with ox-headed and horse-faced demons, wielding iron spears, drive [the beings] into the city gate toward the Avīci Hell.
Therein, two types of contact are manifested: first, contact through conjunction, where mountains press against the body, crushing the bones, flesh, and blood; second, contact through separation.
Swords and blades saw through their bodies; hearts and livers were butchered and torn asunder. When they encountered such things, these could become paths and contemplations, halls and desks.
When they encountered them through sight, these could become burning and blazing. When they encountered them through hearing, these could become striking and clashing, piercing and shooting.
When they encountered them through breathing, these could become caging, bagging, torturing, and binding. When they encountered them through tasting, these could become plowing.
They become tongs; they become axes for cutting and severing. Upon reflection, they can cause one to fall or fly, and to be boiled or roasted.

Thus do karmic actions and their retributions intersect and meet. I and the assembly, since beginningless time, have perhaps craved flowery patterns, silks, brocades, fine gauze, furs from beasts, silk from cocoons, woolen blankets, leather boots, Wu-lin damask, Shu-silk, pepper-colored silk, fox-fur robes, and the seven treasures.
Resplendent garments and fine, smooth silk robes touch the senses and delude the mind, giving rise to unwholesome thoughts. Such evils are immeasurable and boundless;
therefore, this very day, we reverently stand before the Triple Gem and lay each one bare, seeking compassionate repentance.

From this moment forth, we shall don the armor of patience, occupy the seat of the emptiness of phenomena, enter the chamber of compassion, and universally transform sentient beings so that we may ascend together [to enlightenment].

Jue'an: Sixth, regarding the retribution summoned by mental karma, when this mental karma intersects with death, as that person's life ends, they first see an evil wind blowing away and destroying the land.
The deceased’s spirit-consciousness is blown upward into the void, then, riding the whirlwind, it falls back down into the Avīci Hell, where its karmic illumination is revealed.
There are two aspects. First is non-awakening: when delusion reaches its extreme, one becomes frantic and runs about without ceasing. Second is awakening:

when one realizes through awareness, there is suffering—an immeasurable searing and burning whose pain is deep and difficult to endure. Through such perverse thoughts, if one binds these perceptions, they can become the directions and the locations;
if one binds these views, they can become the iron mirrors and stands, serving as the reflectors and witnesses; if one binds these hearings, they can become the great... [text ends].

When combined with solidity, they become ice and frost; when combined with earth, they become soil and mist. When congealed through inhalation, they become great fire-wheels, fire-boats, and fire-cages.
When congealed through tasting, they become great wailing, regret, and weeping. When congealed through touch, they can become either large or small.
Within a single day, they undergo ten thousand deaths and ten thousand births, sometimes face up and sometimes face down; these six modes are called "mutual retribution.

All of these arise from the deluded ignorance of sentient beings, with the three poisons as their cause and the ten habitual tendencies as their condition. Thus, cause and condition intersect and converge.
Since the retribution is co-arisen with the cause, we know that the creation of karma is illusory and the reception of retribution is illusory;

all are like flowers in the sky, a disordered cataract obscuring the true nature (*dharmatā*). Yet, within the realm of ultimate principle, there has never been any deviation. These deluded thoughts arise adventitiously and have never been inherently present within the *bodhicitta*.
Therefore, as we are but ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*), how could we know the path of the sages? It may be that [these afflictions] arise due to the three poisons.

Deluded, we may accumulate transgressions through the ten habitual tendencies or commit offenses via the six sense faculties; inevitably, we shall fall into the four realms of existence to wander in saṃsāra.

Therefore, I now seek compassionate repentance. I look up and pray that the Triple Gem of the ten directions, the Ten Wheels, and the Compassionate Honored One Kṣitigarbha will radiate pure light to illuminate us, so that all our faults and misdeeds—both our own and those of others—may be dissolved like ice. May [this merit] be multiplied...
The power of this present repentance increases the Path and diminishes birth, leading ultimately to peace and bliss. By means of adamantine wisdom, it shatters ignorance;
the secret treasury of the mind-ground is perfectly accomplished in accordance with thought, becoming equal to the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and eighteen unique qualities.

Endowed with immeasurable merit and the six supernormal powers, with the three types of penetration clearly manifest and the four analytical knowledges widely proclaimed, they deliver all sentient beings to the end.
Thereafter, entering parinirvāṇa, they have sincerely repented and made vows; now we take refuge and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem.

Praising the ten causes of delusive habituation, one commits sins as vast as mountains. When the six sense faculties deliver their mutual retributions, one falls into the Avīci Hell; who will pity those suffering there?
Prostrate before the compassionate countenance; cause and effect shall repay themselves.

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, I shall next perform repentance. Thus far, I have finished repenting for delusions, karma, and retribution; the three obstacles are now purified.
The three paths have been suspended in their bitterness. Now we shall perform repentance for the remaining transgressions of the three types of beings—those of the hungry ghosts, animals, and humans.
All these sentient beings, throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past, have reviled the codes of discipline, violated the bodhisattva precepts, and defiled the nature of nirvana.

They destroy the root of bodhi. Riding upon the ten causes of habitual practice, they commit immeasurable transgressions: being unfilial toward their parents, acting in opposition to their teachers and elders, and indulging in killing, stealing, and lying at will;
praising themselves while disparaging others; engaging in lewdness and debauchery; and creating all manner of karmic deeds, for which they receive retribution by entering the Avīci Hell.

They undergo ten thousand forms of suffering, burning through successive kalpas; though they endure various intense agonies until their retribution in hell is exhausted, they fall back into the realm of hungry ghosts.

There are ten types of birth within this ghostly destiny. If one’s original habituation was lustful, with a craving for form as the cause, they will be born as male and female ghosts who pursue one another.
Laxity has become the prevailing custom; their transgressions are committed within the prisons of karma. Having passed through kalpas as numerous as motes of dust, they are born into the human realm.

Encountering winds, they become *pǔ* (drought demons), who wither the grain in the fields, scorch the moisture of the air, and dry up the rivers and streams. Driven by the habit of desire, they cause fires to break out in ancestral shrines;

with a lustful mind, they bring about ruin and drowning for their own children. This class of beings is called the *hàn-pú* (drought-demon) ghost. With greed for wealth as their cause, they commit theft.
Having secretly formed these habits, they encroached upon the public for their private gain and did not abandon their stinginess, benefiting themselves at the expense of others.
When the retribution for such karma is exhausted and they emerge from hell, they may attain birth among humans, yet they remain in the realm of ghosts.

They become attached to gold, silver, jade, and silk, or take form by relying on grasses and trees—such as the golden essence playing at Douyi, or the tree spirit striking Cao Mao. This class of beings is called...

He became a malevolent ghost; due to his habitual arrogance, with greed and haughtiness as the cause, he gave rise to mutual defiance, exalting himself and looking down upon others, being self-important and disdainful of all things.
When his body perished and his life ended, he was reborn in the hells for sand-grains of kalpas. Only when his karmic retribution was exhausted did his mind finally conceive the desire to ascend.
Remaining in secluded obscurity, they take form according to their karmic breath; haughty and deluded, they never cease to exist, constantly harboring a hollow hunger.

Even when encountering water, it can still bring them harm. For five hundred years they do not hear the name of drink or food; for thousands of millions of kalpas they perpetually suffer the misery of starvation.
This class of beings is called *preta*, or hungry ghosts. Their greedy habits and recollective karma arise from the mutual conflict of craving.

When encountering those who oppose them, they harbor resentment without forgetting it; they give rise to a mind of anger and hatred, which develops further into fury. The fire of this fury burns through the void and results in rebirth in hell.
Once their retribution for sins is exhausted and they imagine ascending to the human realm, they encounter decline and calamity;

still relying on their resentful energy, they suffer from virulent fevers, consumption, and wasting diseases, such that even in life they are unable to extinguish these thieves, yet at death they manifest a terrifying power.

Such spirits as these are called *lìzhì guǐ* (ghosts of malicious intent). If they originally practiced deception and their nature was inherently crooked, relying on emptiness and constructing falsehoods, being led astray by mutual influence, they will incite evil karma and incur the transgressions of hell. They shall sink for billions of kalpas, suffering without end.

When their emotional attachments are exhausted and their thoughts turn toward ascent, they may briefly be born among humans; yet they take form within the animal realm, falsely claiming knowledge of fortune and misfortune—such as foxes and badgers.
Pigs and dogs; parrots and cranes—such as Gong Yechang in his bonds and Pei Sheng released from his tethering.
This class of beings is called *mei*-ghosts (*māyā*). If one’s original habituation was to deception, and greed and falsehood have formed transgressions;

if one is full of schemes and concealment, seeking profit for oneself, and falsely usurps the authority of the eminent, causing people’s minds to become clouded—then all such strategic maneuvers will fall into their trap. They manifest...
Deluded regarding appearances, they contend with one another over right and wrong; consequently, they undergo the retribution of hell until their karmic emotions wither.

When they seek to ascend to the human realm, they encounter the obscure and take form, yet they still rely upon lying down and sleeping. In their nightmares, they fear others; in the brief moment it takes to cook yellow millet, they find themselves as officials under the *huai* tree for an entire day.
This class of beings is called the "soporific ghosts" (*yàn mèi guǐ*). If their past habits were rooted in greed and resentment, [they manifest accordingly].
Conceiving evil and creating karma, one binds oneself in resentment and becomes an enemy; the retribution of hell accumulates upon oneself, persisting through many kalpas.

When one's afflictions are exhausted and the desire for rebirth arises, one briefly dwells among humans, where one encounters a *gū* (poisonous spirit) that takes form as a strange hybrid of tortoise and snake; its calamities and portents are known beforehand, and its hidden influences remain entangled and persistent.
The retribution for residual habits causes the wisdom of the Bright King to manifest in dreams; their bodies find it difficult to escape from cauldrons and boiling pots.

Such a class as this is called the "Poisonous Charm Ghost" (*gudu-ghost*). If one’s original habitual tendencies obscure the mind and form karma, then regarding the inner and outer orthodox scriptures, heterodox views arise.
Although they engage in the weaving of affairs, their births are constantly contrary; they deny cause and effect and reject the permanence of the precepts, falling into hell.

In the midst [of this state], when their emotional attachments have reached their limit and they conceive the thought of ascending, they then enter the realm of ghosts. Meeting with light, they take form. There are those who encounter solar and lunar eclipses, or mountain and marsh spirits;
there are those who employ yellow stones and talismans in secret arts, or who find subtle efficacy in the profound instructions of the *Qing Na*.

This class of beings is called the *Wǎnglǎng* (Māyāvin) ghosts. Due to the causes of past habits, greed becomes the condition for their existence; through the karma of deception and falsehood, they perversely associate with shamans and spirit-mediums, promoting all manner of crookedness.

They were perverse and straightforward in their conduct; they deceived others with their own persons and brought harm and distress to the innocent. Their crimes have been testified to and recorded, yet they continue to create evil, for which they shall receive retribution in the Avīci Hell.

When their karmic conditions are exhausted and their thoughts ascend, they will be reborn among humans as lowly servants and laborers—carrying stones and shifting sand, damming ravines and filling rivers, driving mountains by whip into the sea.
This was like the Money Kings shooting at water-spirits, or the First Emperor of Qin plotting against the mountain deities. Thus it is.
There is a class known as the *yǒngshǐ guǐ* (servant-demon). Due to the habitual tendencies of past lives, they form greedy factions and gather in swarms;

they expose the hidden evils of others and establish cliques with their own wicked kindred. Such is the way they commit transgressions. When their punishment in hell has ended and their karmic conditions have exhausted, they seek rebirth in the human realm.

Upon being transmitted and taking form, they are like those who assist spirit-boards in the world, or shamans, sorcerers, and children’s playthings, performing divinations of good and ill fortune, and indicating blessings, calamities, misfortunes, and blessings.
Observing the interplay of yin and yang, although the nine schools of thought demonstrate ways of seeking refuge and avoiding danger, they all fall into partiality and deviation.

This class of beings is called the "transmitting ghosts. Thus, these ten classes of ghostly persons all arise from delusion regarding the Truth and pursuit of the false; they are conjured by illusion and formed through illusion.

They falsely construct right and wrong, all following their emotional attachments and perceptions. Having incurred the retribution of hell, they return to the realm of ghosts, where the fires of karma sear them.
The retribution for these deeds has been largely exhausted, yet the lingering traces have not yet run dry; thus I have fallen among the ten classes of beings.
Therefore, today, in reverent presence of the Triple Gem and the Compassionate Honored One Kṣitigarbha, I lay each matter bare and repent again and again.

May the ten habitual practices of the past be entirely eliminated and wiped away, and may I never again receive a ghostly body in the future. Having escaped the suffering of the dark and submerged realms, may I roam freely according to my vows.

Wandering through life, we practice in every thought-moment; with every mind directed toward the path of goodness, may we together attain the sudden realization of the Dharma, reaching even unto Bodhi.

May the source of worldly passions be forever severed, and may we long sail upon the ocean of awakening. I and this assembly, with renewed sincerity, prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground, taking refuge and paying homage to all Buddhas.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha. Homage to Amitābha Buddha.
Homage to Sarvajñatāsiddhi Buddha. Homage to Mahāprabha Buddha.
Homage to Padmaviśuddhanetra Buddha. Homage to Samādhiprabha Buddha.
Homage to the Buddha Wisdom Radiance. Homage to the Buddha Merit Radiance.
Homage to the Buddha Virtue Radiance. Homage to the Buddha Kāṣāya Banner.
Homage to the Buddha Lion’s Roar Sovereign King. Homage to the Buddha Awakening Flower Sovereign King.
Homage to the Buddha Siṃhavikrīḍitaparipūrṇasarvacaryā.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. Homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati; homage to the Bodhisattva Vasumitra;
homage to the Honored One, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.
Having paid obeisance to all the Buddhas, we now proceed to repent. We have already finished repenting for the offenses of the realm of hungry ghosts; we shall now repent for our own transgressions.

This is the transgression that leads to the animal realm. The reason for this is that when the prison of punishment exhausts one's emotions and the retribution of ghosts depletes one's perceptions, both emotions and perceptions—these two delusions—become simultaneously empty.
Only then does one emerge from the human world, yet immediately enters the animal realm, where one encounters those to whom one was originally indebted as karmic adversaries.

To repay the karmic debts of former lives, there are also ten kinds of beings among the various classes of animals (*tiryagyoni*). When these monstrous spirits exhaust their material substance and their forms perish, they are reborn among humans, mostly as owls.
Because they have not yet eliminated their residual habits, they greedily take clods of earth for children and carry insects in their beaks as offspring;
such uniformities of strange anomalies are all among the beasts. I now openly confess and repent on their behalf, so that their past habits may be extinguished.

Excluding those who, by virtue of the compassionate power of the Earth Store Bodhisattva, have been liberated from suffering like the *xiāo* bird, and have ultimately realized their fundamental source and attained mastery over the mind.
As for the ghosts of wind and drought, when the wind subsides and the ghosts are extinguished, they will be reborn among humans, where they often manifest as omens of calamity:

flocks of sparrows signal scarcity; swarms of rats cry out in times of desolation; *shāng-niǎo* birds bring forth water; stone-swallows respond to the wind; cranes dance during prolonged droughts; and rainbows appear...

The objects on the shelves have vanished; their varieties are not one, all collectively termed "ominous omens. May you now reveal your transgressions, emerge from the ranks of the deluded, attain mastery over the Dharma, and transcend to higher realms according to your vows.
As for those who flatter spirits, they will perish as livestock or as dead things; if they are reborn among humans, [they shall suffer accordingly].

Deceitful habits take form; as a ghost, one remains sycophantic and fawning. Once that basis is extinguished, one undergoes rebirth as a fox. Belonging to the category of cats and wildcats, one begs for sustenance by relying on humans;

seeking aid through a thousand acts of flattery, such beings are collectively termed "fox-animals. By virtue of repentance now, one moves to receive the Buddha’s grace, eliminating the causal conditions of past habituation so that the fruit of such karma shall not be received hereafter.
As for those of the *gǔ* (demoness/pestilence) class, once their poison is neutralized and their forms perish, they will be reborn among humans.
For a time, they are still called members of the animal realm. Vipers, snakes, vipers, and scorpions; hidden dragons, tigers, and leopards;

and stinging wasps that bite humans—such karmic habits of enmity revolve and are difficult to forget. By the power of the repentance of [Name] and others, may they escape their non-human bodies as beings of different species;
gradually may they accord with the Truth and not sink into delusion and falsehood. Furthermore, we repent: may the ghosts of decay and pestilence be released from birth among humans and be named...

The class of *kṛmi* (worms) is driven by the habit-energy of anger; as ghosts, they cause pestilence and decay within the bodies of humans, and upon returning to the realm of animals, they again take birth therein as *kṛmi*, *ārśas*, and other such parasites.

Because the habit-energy of anger is stubborn and obdurate, the retribution of an animal takes the form of a soft-bodied insect. Thus, cause and effect encounter one another, turning over in an instant.
May all such habitual tendencies be confessed and eliminated; through the compassionate grace of the Buddha, may one immediately attain peace of mind and receive [this teaching].

The ghosts of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) arise because their breath has dissipated from material objects; they are reborn among humans, all belonging to the class of the greedy. Greed and arrogance are their cause, while hunger and emptiness are their fruit.
Their bodies are provided for the kitchen, hence they are called the "class of eaters. Their skin and flesh fill the offerings, and their bones and marrow serve as meals.

Fish, shellfish, furred birds, chickens, geese, fish, turtles, oxen, sheep, and pigs—all suffer unjustly at the hands of knives and blockades. This is the lingering residue of the habit of arrogance, sinking [into this state].

Sinking into the retribution of animals—such beings as these are to be repented for on their behalf. All their karmic offenses resulting from wrongful deeds are completely purified, like ice melting away.
If they were ghosts dwelling in the darkness, their spirits vanish and their obscurity is extinguished; when reborn in the human realm, they mostly become members of the domesticated animal class.

While as ghosts they suffered from lingering entanglements and became sources of nightmares and malevolent influences, once that gloom has dissolved, they manifest clearly as domestic animals: camels, donkeys, oxen, horses, silkworms, cocoons, and sable.
The fur cloak is dark and hidden, lacking clarity; thus it falls into a different category. Deceptive habituation is the cause; thus one receives the fruit of its corresponding clothing.
Relying now on the power of repentance, I wash away past causes and conditions. Taking refuge in the great grace of Kṣitigarbha, I shall attain the ultimate bliss of the heavenly kin.

With a calm and continuous mind, I shall illumine the unconditioned nature, reach the land of Bodhi, and emerge from the sea of birth and death. Next, I again perform repentance with harmonious vigor.
These ghosts, seeing the habitual causes from former lives, have now become members of the animal realm. Yet they still know the seasonal cycles: the purple swallows return in spring;

the yellow orioles arrive at the summer solstice; the frost-swans migrate back in autumn; and the snow-sparrows linger as they take refuge in winter. Thus, the forms of the frog and the magpie intersect.
The dragonfly is of a different nature; it changes with the passing seasons and is reborn according to its kind.

As for the spirits of the enlightened and the numinous, when their light fades and their souls dissolve, they are born into the human world as auspicious omens. Because they ride upon the power of past practices, they take birth through the clarity of their enlightenment to act as messengers.

When their karmic destiny in the realm of ghosts is exhausted, their animal retribution gives way to auspicious signs. When prosperity is about to arrive, there are premonitory indications; such is the case with the phoenix.

The Zhou dynasty arose from the emergence of the *xing* (unicorn). The birth of a *lin* (qilin) portends the production of a sage. Woodpeckers in the forest herald human joy; spiders descending signify auspicious blessings.

Such occurrences as these are all termed "auspicious omens. Now, I prostrate and repent before the Dharma to cleanse my past causes, suddenly restore the clarity of my mind, and return to the fundamental nature of the ground.
May I forever rely upon the holy teachings, not fall into saṃsāra, and wondrously accord with the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), entering [Nirvāṇa].
The Heart-Mind Treasury is a ghost that depends upon man; when man perishes, the ghost is extinguished. Having been born into this world, it mostly follows the category of domesticated creatures.

Through the causes of habitual litigation, the ghost is summoned and dispatched. Now it has become an animal, yet its retributive substance is clever and wise, possessing the beautiful resonance of the kalaviṅka bird.
The parrot is skilled in speech; the crane can recite the Buddha’s words; the monkey imitates humans. Though these are called "spiritual birds," they are kept as domestic pets by men.

Yet these ten aforementioned classes [of beings] all result from deluded emotions that have frozen into ice and karmic habits that have been intensely summoned. They are wrongly pursued through the three miserable realms, where the fires of karma are endless.
When the water of emotion has dried up by the heat, one must repay former debts even while remaining an animal. Because they are kept by humans, they are thus named.
The forms of animals are lateral; because they move laterally, they are called "lateral-born beings. All are summoned and manifested by deluded karma.
Within the secret treasury of the mind-ground, these are all but empty flowers. Upon the substance of empty flowers, how could there exist any real fruit? Therefore, I have come here now.
[I,] [Name], together with the assembly, first repent for the realm of ghosts, and next regret [the karma of] the animal realm.

May we all aspire to awaken together to the ten habitual false causes, and immediately realize together the true fruit of the One Vehicle. Furthermore, one should know that the aforementioned ghosts and animals each repay their former debts.
When their retribution is exhausted, they return once more to the human realm. Within the human realm, there are likewise ten kinds of distinctions.

If, in past lives, one had previously incurred another's debts of wealth or labor and has now repaid them in full and ceased [the cycle], yet in a prior existence had taken that person's life or eaten their flesh—and if this continues even through kalpas as numerous as motes of dust, with mutual devouring and slaughter like [the following]— [The text continues: ...just as... (as in the preceding analogy).
The well-wheel turns, with its buckets rising and falling in alternation; until the end of time, it can never be stopped.
Were it not for this repentance, when could liberation be expected? Therefore, we [Name et al. prostrate with a sincere heart, confessing our faults, seeking mercy, and offering our apologies.
Once past karma is purified, one shall ascend to the human realm. Indeed, for those born into the human path, the constant observance of precepts serves as the primary cause and condition. Now...

When the sufferings of the three miserable realms have ended, one may also attain human birth. Yet there are those who are foolish enough to say: "Once the suffering of evil karma has exhausted itself, one naturally becomes a human being;
why is it necessary to cultivate goodness and plant roots of merit to create the virtuous path for humans and devas? If one harbors such thoughts, their transgression is truly not light.

However, although those in the human realm share the same general retribution for their existence, they differ vastly in terms of wisdom and folly; thus, there are ten distinctions between the noble and the lowly.

Now, as the retributions of the three miserable paths have been exhausted, it is said that they have "ascended. This is merely the reception of residual karma in a secondary manner and is certainly not born from primary causes and conditions.
Therefore, the Sūtra says: "The names are designated as a composite. You all should know that as for those of the class of owls, they are a recompense for...

Their feet have regained their form, and they are born among the human race; yet they are mixed with the dull and stubborn, for due to their greed for material things, ghosts assume monstrous forms, and among animals there are the earth-owl and the like.
Now, though they possess human bodies, their nature is ignorant and deluded; they are mixed with the obstinate and the stupid.

Their minds lack virtue and righteousness, and how could their wills preserve benevolence? They are unfilial and disloyal, lacking integrity and shame; they indulge in clamor at will because of the habits of greed.

As for those who manifest such portents of retribution, once their karmic debt is fully repaid, they take form again within the human realm; they are born amidst the dull and ignorant, possessing the habitual tendencies of greed and lust from former lives.

Having previously suffered as ghosts or *pǔ* spirits, or ascending to the state of animals, these are the responses to their calamities and transgressions. When their karma is exhausted and they return to human status, they remain as foolish and deluded as before.

Because they are attached to lustful desires, they do not cultivate other virtues; thus, they invite dullness and stupidity. Knowing what is good, they do not follow it; their instructions are met with defiance;
they turn their backs on the rules and go against the laws, acting like those who are drunk or insane. Therefore, they are called "foolish and crude.

As for those of the fox lineage, once their retribution is exhausted and they regain a physical form, they are born among human beings. They are characterized by a mixture of ferocity and deceit; they practice the arts of litigation and fraud as ghosts, and rely on flattery as their mode of being—belonging to the eight classes of marginal spirits.

Born as a fox, now they have entered the human realm; yet they are characterized by a mixture of ferocity and cruelty, being stubborn and self-willed, refusing the counsel of others and acting only according to their own arbitrary whims—truly base and vulgar men.
As for those who were poisonous vermin, once their retribution has ended, they resume their forms and are born into the human path, mingling with the ranks of common laborers.
Habitual resentment is the cause, and the poison of the vermin is the fruit. In the animal realm of the side-born, they become vipers and snakes.
This form has now returned as a human body, yet it is filled with various lowly and menial tasks, driven by others and enduring hunger and cold;

these are the lingering karmic retributions of the past, inviting such base and humble status today. As for those like the *āhri* worms, though born within the human realm, they are but a minute and mixed class.

With greed and gluttony as their habitual practice, they suffer the decay and pestilence of a ghostly retribution; they become animals such as *ārśas* and *āhri* worms, or humans who are so weak and frail that they are not even counted among the ranks of men.
From cold and heat, they depend on others for satiety or hunger; their stubbornness turns to suppleness as cause and effect play in alternation.

Those who partook of food have their retribution fulfilled and shall likewise regain their form, being reborn among humans and integrated into the category of the supple. Yet, the habitual causes of greed and arrogance remain.

The hungry ghosts experience their karmic fruit: empty bellies and haughty minds, lacking any substantial nature. Reborn as animals, they consume the common provisions; when reborn as humans, they are weak and pliant.
This is likely because of their arrogance that invited such timidity. The distinction between strength and weakness is stark—who would be willing to believe it?

You, having served your peers and fulfilled your obligations, shall again take form and be born into the human realm, joining the ranks of the weary. These causes of delusion and deception lead to the state of a ghost in the dark.

The *yàn* (demon of nightmares): animals endure servitude and patience; humans undergo toil and exertion, laboring with hardship. Among the various crafts and skills, amidst the multitude of diverse affairs, they are driven by cold and heat;

hence they are called the "category of labor. Furthermore, regarding those who correspond to the human realm: having received a full recompense as a person, they participate in and harmonize with civilization.

Due to their accumulated habits (*vāsanā*), they descend as ghosts with refined spirits; when their retribution as *wǎngliǎng* (sprites) ends, they summon their animal nature to respond to external objects. Thus they participate in and harmonize with [the world].
In the human realm, there is an abundance of literary renown; this is not due to primary causes and conditions, but is thus termed a "confluence.
As for auspicious omens, these likewise pertain to humans; they clarify the relations between people, while the origins of habitual training reveal the retributions of spiritual efficacy.

Driven and employed without a moment’s rest, animals may be summoned to exhibit cleverness, while humans receive the gift of intelligence. Examining the past and seeking the present, there is not the slightest discrepancy.

Those who follow this ethical sequence repay their debts and restore humanity, participating among the enlightened class. Due to the habituation of litigation, the retribution of ghosts relies upon humans;

through talismans and incantations, words are transmitted, and curses manifest fortune or calamity. Animal retribution stems from past causes, while humans understand the extremes of poverty and success. Thus, they are not startled by honor or disgrace.

They still know how to advance and retreat; like those who abstain from grain in deep mountains, or those who ride upon rafts across the vast ocean—such as these belong to one class, and are thus called "those who have attained the Way.
However, these ten aforementioned types all belong to past kalpas; they had not yet heard the Buddha-dharma and did not rely on the cultivation of the Sangha.

Driven by the delusive causes of the ten habitual tendencies, one creates the ten kinds of severe karma and undergoes illusory suffering in the hells. When one's emotions are exhausted and thoughts ascend, one returns to the realm of ghosts.
When the retribution of the ghost realm is exhausted, one returns again to the animal realm. When the retribution of the animal realm ends, one eventually regains a human body.

Although they possess human bodies, these ten types are utterly distinct; all arise from deluded attachments and inversions, with the ten *anuśayas* (latent tendencies) acting as conditions, leading them to commit the ten non-virtuous actions.
You owe me my life, while I owe you my wealth; thus we harm one another and kill one another, acting falsely and doing what is unreal.

Having failed to encounter the Buddha Vehicle and not having heard the wholesome Dharma, they remain far removed from the practice of the Sangha, relying solely on the causes of their habitual tendencies. Amidst the dust and toil of worldly existence, this is their natural state.

In this cycle of saṃsāra, how could one avoid the words of the Buddha? This is truly pitiable. Therefore, I now follow the teachings bestowed by the Triple Gem and rely upon the perfect scripture of Kṣitigarbha.

I shall manifest the power of vows of universal compassion to repent for the habitual causes shared with all beings—from the three delusions and the six sense faculties, up to the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, as well as the three paths of rebirth and the perilous realms within the triple world.

Rising and sinking, coming and going, we have not yet attained liberation. We look up with hope that the Three Jewels and the holy sages will deign to grant their witness to our repentance, so that our long-standing obscurations may be eliminated, the three delusions may be suddenly emptied, the three contemplations may become perfectly luminous, and the three truths may be instantaneously revealed.
May the ten bodies be fully realized in this present life, and the ten realms together attain eternal bliss. Following all the Bodhisattvas, may we sever delusions and realize [enlightenment].
Truly. Having completed the repentance, I take refuge in and pay homage to all Buddhas, as well as to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha.
Homage to our Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha; homage to Amitābha Buddha;
homage to the Honored Buddha Maitreya; homage to the Seven Buddhas of the Past.
Homage to the ten Buddhas of the ten directions; homage to the thirty-five Buddhas;
homage to the fifty-three Buddhas; homage to the one hundred and seventy Buddhas;
homage to the thousand Buddhas of the *Vyuha-kalpa*; homage to the thousand Buddhas of the *Bhadrakalpa*.
Homage to the thousand Buddhas of the Constellation Kalpa. Homage to all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Homage to all Buddhas within the *Kṣitigarbha Sūtra*.
Homage to all the great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions. Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Homage to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
Homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva. Homage to Akṣayamati Bodhisattva.
Homage to Gaganagañja Bodhisattva. Homage to Ajita Bodhisattva.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Anantagātra; homage to the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.

Having paid homage to all the Buddhas, one next performs repentance. Thus far, one has repented of the three obstructions, the ten evil deeds, the retributions of the six sense organs, and the various remaining retributions within the realms of ghosts, animals, and humans. By the power of this repentance, delusions and karma are completely purified and eliminated.

As for the fruits of retribution, may they never again be committed. I vow that those in the six realms and four modes of birth shall each be fully endowed with merit, wisdom, spiritual powers, and the scope of their vows, so that they may, like Bodhisattvas, attain mastery according to their will.
The *Kṣitigarbha-pūrvapraṇidhāna-sūtra* states: "In future ages, if there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, good men, good women, boys, or girls who are not themselves..."

Furthermore, those who hear my name, behold my image, burn incense, scatter flowers, make offerings to the World-Honored One, and prostrate themselves in repentance—not only shall they eliminate the causes of their past sins and the resulting suffering, but within this very lifetime, they shall obtain twenty kinds of supreme and wondrous benefits.
First, they shall be protected by devas and nāgas, and no illnesses shall arise. Second...
1. Virtuous fruits increase daily, and blessings overflow with further prosperity. 2. The three roots of goodness are firmly planted, blossoming into flowers and bearing fruit.
3. Food and clothing are abundant and sufficient, never inviting poverty or want. 4. Calamities and disasters are eliminated, and body and mind are relaxed and joyful.
5. One is spared from the calamities of water and fire, dwelling always in peace. 6. Thieves and bandits do not invade, and the smoke of war is extinguished. 7. [The eighth:]...

1. People will see them with reverence and respect; they will follow the Way and practice benevolence. 2. They will repay their karmic debts from former lives, bringing peace and joy to body and mind. 3.

Their deceased ancestors will attain liberation, and their lineage will remain fragrant for generations. 4. Women will transform their female bodies into male ones and will not be born in remote or barbarian regions. 5.

When their retribution is exhausted, they will be reborn in the heavens, as they have practiced the ten wholesome deeds. 6. They will possess the supernormal power of knowledge of past lives and will diligently cultivate the True Teaching. 14.
15. All that is sought shall be attained; one’s intentions will be fulfilled and perfected. 16. One’s retinue will be healthy and peaceful; anxieties and misfortunes will be silenced. 17.

All injustices will be dissolved and forgotten; one’s conduct and station will be upright and auspicious. 18. In both waking and sleeping, the spirit will be at ease; body and mind will be sharp and keen. 19.
One’s own and others’ lifespans will be forever free from stumbling and downfall. 20. One will not regress from Bodhi, and the fruits of the Path will gradually be realized.
Practicing charity and compassion, one will ultimately attain Buddhahood. Therefore, today I lead all those of pure faith to take refuge in the Triple Gem.
May the Compassionate Honored One, Kṣitigarbha, bear witness to my heart and fulfill its aspirations. All the various manifestations described above have thus appeared accordingly.
Furthermore, from time immemorial until this very day, due to craving and false views, we have internally clung to the notions of self and person while externally following evil companions;
we have been indolent and lazy, unable to cultivate practice with diligence or to rejoice in wholesome dharmas, remaining mired in doubt regarding both phenomena and principle.
Therefore, I now resolve my mind and rejoice in this ultimate goodness, celebrating both myself and others. To celebrate oneself is to have no contradiction with the Principle;

to celebrate others is to engage in the cultivation of deeds and the refinement of the mind. By following the Principle, one can accord with the two primordial Awakenings of the beginning and the source; by engaging in deeds, one can harmonize the ten suchnesses of object and wisdom.
Thus, on this day, I resolve my mind and rejoice that all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, as well as those of the Two Vehicles...
I rejoice in all the merits of those in training and those beyond training, as well as all the merits of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
(Having rejoiced, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem and the Compassionate Honored One Kṣitigarbha, rising to perform one prostration.)
Furthermore, take refuge in the Triple Gem of the ten directions and vow to be born among all Bodhisattvas;
having rejoiced with a sympathetic heart, they should then entreat the Triple Gem of the ten directions and the noble ones of the ten stages to remain forever in the world.
These noble sages have taught and transformed us, bringing benefit to all classes of beings; therefore, today with a sincere heart, I entreat you:

O Lamps of the World throughout the ten directions, who first attained the realization of Bodhi, may you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in the lands, for the sake of benefiting and gladdening all sentient beings. (The prayer of entreaty is as above.)

Furthermore, one takes refuge in these Three Jewels. Having completed the preceding acts of repentance, sympathetic joy, and entreaty, one should now give rise to the mind of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*).
Why is this so? That all sentient beings are unable to dwell freely in liberation is entirely due to their attachment to karmic retribution;
because of this, they are unable to relinquish it. Whatever virtue there may be, even as small as a single hair’s breadth, can be dedicated.
Enlightenment (bodhi) means that the wholesome karma one has cultivated is no longer bound by attachment; thus, the affairs of saṃsāra are severed. As a sutra says:

"Cultivating practice and dedicating it brings about the great fruit of merit. I now dedicate even this slight wholesome merit I have cultivated, while also exhorting all others not to remain greedily attached.
All my repentances, as well as my sympathetic joy, requests [for the Buddhas to remain], and the causes and conditions thereof, I entirely dedicate. Nature...

Characterizing the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha; the seal of samādhi wherein the two truths are harmoniously integrated—such an ocean of wisdom and merit, I dedicate to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha (having dedicated as before).

Furthermore, having taken refuge in the Three Jewels and the Noble Ones, and having completed the cultivation of the mind of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*), one should now resolve upon the aspiration for unexcelled bodhi.
As the Sūtra says: "If there is aspiration but no practice, that aspiration will surely be empty; if there is practice but no aspiration, that practice is likewise delusive.
How can empty and delusive aspirations and practices ever achieve their fruit? Therefore, on this day, I ought to make great vows, so that through these vows [practice] may be assisted."
Practice. Practice assists the fulfillment of vows; through the perfect cultivation of practice and vows, one accords with the wondrous fruit of truth.

By means of these causes and conditions of the merit of such vows and practice, may each and every person be fully endowed with wisdom and supernormal powers. May the practices and vows of all Buddhas be fulfilled from the heart.

Furthermore, I vow that in birth after birth and in every place throughout the ages, through the compassion of the Buddhas, I shall deliver all sentient beings from the sufferings of the three miserable realms and grant them—
May all sentient beings attain the joy of the two kinds of goodness, reach ultimate bodhi, and accomplish the unsurpassed path.
Furthermore, I vow that in every birth and in every place throughout all lifetimes, may all sentient beings have their ignorance and afflictions severed without remainder.

May the three truths be clearly manifested. Furthermore, may it be my vow that in every birth and in every place, all sentient beings shall, through hearing, contemplation, and cultivation, penetrate deeply into all dharma-gates without exception.

Moreover, may it be my vow that in every birth and in every place, all sentient beings shall attain faith, understanding, practice, and realization regarding the unsurpassed noble path, and open, reveal, awaken to, and enter the Buddha’s [wisdom].
With knowledge and vision, they realize the ultimate permanence, bliss, self, and purity, clearly manifesting the secret treasury of the mind-ground and entering therein.
Furthermore, they vow that in every birth and in every place, throughout all lands where they may be born, they shall always encounter righteous kings and crown princes.
May the office of the Minister flourish and manifest the Buddha-dharma; may he revere the Mahāyāna and encourage and guide the śramaṇas, extensively carrying out the work of transformation.
Furthermore, may it be vowed that in birth after birth and in every place, may [so-and-so] and others be fully endowed with the three arts, both internal and external, in a single thought-moment.
The three contemplations are perfectly clear and bright; the three truths are suddenly revealed. Having reached the ultimate ground of the mind, one finally ascends to the secret treasury.

Furthermore, I vow that in birth after birth and in place after place, riding upon the power of the Bodhisattvas, I shall take birth in this Sahā world and other realms, propagating the Buddha-way above and transforming sentient beings below, until we ultimately attain perfect permanence and together return to quiescent extinction. The preceding repentance is now concluded.

I make this vow: as vast as the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), ultimately equal to space, and extending to the furthest reaches of the future, may I fulfill the vow for enlightenment and enter the secret treasury together with all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
This *Praise of the Kṣitigarbha Repentance Method* consists of three complete fascicles. Its grace sustains the nine realms of existence and bestows benefit upon humans and devas;
its welfare is vast and boundless, and its merit is profoundly mysterious. May it be perpetually transmitted.
Homage to Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva (recite three times).
